plaintiff.education_level: Higher Diploma from the Institute of Vocational Education; Bachelor of Arts Degree

injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the knee or lower leg

injuries.description: complete tear of the ACL close to the femoral insertion
source: The MRI revealed a complex tear involving the anterior horn, body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus and a complete tear of the ACL close to the femoral insertion.

manifestations.description: tenderness over medial side of left knee
Lachman’s test and pivot shift test were positive
residual wasting of his left lower limb
difficulty playing football / reduced enjoyment of sports
limping (observed on surveillance video and in evidence)

treatments_received.treatment: Ambulance to Accident and Emergency Department of Tuen Mun Hospital; A&E examination
source: The plaintiff was taken by ambulance to the Accident and Emergency Department of Tuen Mun Hospital. Examination revealed no fracture but tenderness over medial side of left knee. He was given sick leave and discharged.
The plaintiff was referred to and did have an MRI on 3 April 2012.
The MRI revealed a complex tear involving the anterior horn, body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus and a complete tear of the ACL close to the femoral insertion.

treatments_received.treatment: ACL reconstruction and partial medial meniscectomy with left knee arthroscopy (4-hour surgery)
source: The next day, he underwent a 4-hour surgery involving ACL reconstruction and partial medial meniscectomy with left knee arthroscopy.

The plaintiff was then admitted on 18 April 2012 to St Teresa’s Hospital. The next day, he underwent a 4-hour surgery ... He was hospitalised for 5 days until 22 April 2012. He was discharged walking with a pair of clutches.

treatments_received.treatment: Physiotherapy (31 sessions at North District Hospital)
source: Since 14 June 2012, the plaintiff has been receiving physiotherapy treatments from North District Hospital until 23 January 2013 for a total of 31 sessions.

treatments_received.treatment: Follow-up consultations with Dr Raymond Lai (25 visits)
source: The plaintiff since then has been followed up by Dr Lai until he was last seen on 14 January 2013. The plaintiff was seen by Dr Lai for a total of 25 times.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: The plaintiff has a sense of uneasiness with jogging, difficulty in full squat, walking downstairs and playing football; the enjoyment of sports by the plaintiff would be reduced.
